correctness.rationale: On circle i the approaching-circle factor is ε(2r_j+ε)+2r_i(1−cos t), where t is measured from prospective contact. The other speed factors are uniformly nonzero. Scaling t by sqrt(2R_j ε/R_i) gives an integrable bound proportional to (1+z²)⁻¹ on the rescaled reciprocal-speed density, yielding both prefactors and both Cauchy laws by normalization. Circle 3 has uniformly nonzero limiting speed. Taking the radial derivative of f_i gives the stated cofactors; in the only near-singular quotient the numerator is sin(t) times a smooth factor with a uniformly bounded derivative. Pairing t and −t makes it O(t²), so the quotient is bounded by C t²/(ε+t²); positive-time orientation has constant sign and dominated convergence applies. Dividing the finite log limits by the physical periods gives the stated rate. The explicit contact values are 106/25, 4, and −3 and yield ratio 4/3. 'Two distinct clocks' means two orbits; their prefactors need not differ in general. Frozen symbolic checks and two-gap quadratures corroborate identities and examples, not the limiting proof.
